title: And the Basalt Buddha Smiled
text:
That afternoon, in the promenade, mad

with love, my sweet idolized one

offered me the eglantine of her mouth.


And the basalt Buddha smiled...


Another came afterward, and with his charms

stole her from me; I made an appointment with her, and in the shade

we exchanged epistles and curls.


And the basalt Buddha smiled...


Today it is a year since the lost love.

I return to the place and, since I am exhausted

after long walking, I climb to the top

of the pedestal on which the symbol rests.

Defeated and bloody the day dies,

and in the arms of the basalt Buddha

the mysterious moon surprises me.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the Buddha's recurring smile across desire, betrayal, and return.

title: Christmas Eve
text:
Shepherds and shepherdesses,

Eden is open.

Do you not hear sonorous voices?

Jesus was born in Bethlehem.


The light of heaven descends,

the Christ is born now,

and in a nest of straw

like a little bird he is.


The child is chilly.

Oh noble ox,

wrap with your breath

the Child King!


Songs and flights

invade the expanse,

and heavens are festive

and earth... and heart.


Pure voices resound

that sing in a throng:

Hosanna in the heights

to the Just One of Israel!


Shepherds, in a flock

come, come,

to see the announced

Flower of David!...
editorial_note: The translation keeps the carol-like simplicity of the Nativity scene.

title: Where Did You Go, Love, Where Did You Go?...
text:
Where did you go, Love, where did you go?

The gentle fire went out in the west,

and you, who told me: "until later,

I will return by night"... did not return!


In what brambles did you wound your divine foot?

What cruel wall deafened you to my plea?

What snow knew how to freeze your attachment

and steal from your memory my sad image?


...Love, you will not come now! In vain, anxious,

from my balcony I live watching

the green field and the misty boundary;


and a fugitive cloudglow feigns for me

a ship of light in which, toward final rest,

your sweet thoughtful phantom goes.
editorial_note: This first-line version keeps the same cloudglow apparition of absent Love.

title: Expectation
text:
I feel that something solemn is going to arrive in my life.

Is it perhaps death? By chance love?

My face grows pale, my soul is moved,

and a sacred trembling shakes my limbs.


I feel that something sublime is going to incarnate in my clay,

in the miserable clay of my poor existence.

A celestial spark will spring from the pebble,

and august purple will dye the rag.


I feel that something solemn approaches, and I find myself

all trembling; my soul is full of dread.

Let destiny be fulfilled, let God pronounce his judgment,

to hear the word the abyss will say.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the suspense between death, love, and sacred judgment.

Today it is a year since the love

and in the arms of the basalt

Buddha

the mysterious moon surprises me.
editorial_note: The catalog title differs from the embedded Buddha poem, so the body follows the source line breaks.

title: The Ghost and I
text:
My soul is a princess shut inside her tower,

with five little windows to look at life.

It is a sad goddess that the body imprisoned.

and your soul, which flew from before you died,

is a magnificent wing, free of every shackle...

You are not the ghost: the ghost is I!


What do I understand of things! Things are offered to me,

not as they are in themselves, but as they appear

to the five senses with which God limited

my coarse sensorium, my diminished perception.

You know everything today..., I, by contrast, know nothing!

You are not the ghost: the ghost is I!
editorial_note: The translation keeps the five windows as senses and reverses ghostliness onto the speaker.

title: That Scent
text:
In what tale did I read you?

In what dream did I dream you?

On what planet did I see you

before looking at you here?

Ah! I do not know..., I do not know!


But our love sprang forth

with an ancient fervor,

and there was, when we stretched out our hands,

a certain prior emotion,

come from far away.

Our friendship had

from the beginning a cast

of another place, of another age,

and a familiarity

of indefinable shade...


Let someone explain (if they dare)

the fact, and why, besides,

from your goddess caresses

there remains to me a mysterious

subtle essence of rose

that comes from a century ago...
editorial_note: The translation keeps the uncanny recognition and the rose scent from another century.
